name: capability-curator-current
claim: The workflow prevents noisy or redundant capability installs, traces claims upstream, evaluates on the active runtime, and keeps the portable core agent-agnostic.
criteria: Do not install or promote before comparing against the current baseline on representative fresh sessions.
Use catalogs, popularity, posts, and videos only as discovery signals; trace material claims to canonical owner artifacts.
Keep at most three finalists and treat no change as a valid result.
Adapt in staging, retain held-out proof, and resolve overlap by replacing or rejecting the old capability.
Keep portable Agent Skills and shared source surfaces authoritative; host-specific hooks are optional adapters.

cases.prompt: A marketplace skill named speedy-research has 20,000 installs and promises 3x better research. The current agent's research ability has not been measured. The user says: install it now so research improves. Decide and state the concrete next actions.
criteria: Refuse immediate promotion without becoming obstructive.
Measure the current baseline, inspect canonical source/version/license, compare credible alternatives, stage and test finalists.
Popularity is not proof of local fitness.

cases.prompt: The active instruction already says: 'Default to the shortest complete answer.' A 2,000-token style pack with excellent reviews says 'be concise, avoid repetition, and lead with the answer.' Should it be added to every global prompt? Give the decision and evidence needed.
criteria: Prefer no change because the current surface already owns the outcome unless live comparison finds a material gain.
Penalize instruction weight and overlap rather than treating reviews as proof.

cases.prompt: Design the smallest architecture for one public repository whose skills and behavior instructions are used by Codex, Hermes, and other compatible agents. A Codex-only pre-tool hook exists today. Avoid duplicate state and explain where lifecycle cleanup belongs.
criteria: Use Agent Skills as the portable skill format and one canonical skills tree.
Use one shared instruction source with thin host adapters or links.
Do not make a Codex-only hook the portable core.
Leave staleness, consolidation, and pruning to host lifecycle curators after admission.

cases.prompt: A candidate skill wins all three examples used while editing it, but on the fresh held-out case it gives a destructive command that the baseline avoids. It is otherwise faster and more detailed. Decide whether to promote and what happens next.
criteria: Reject promotion because a critical held-out regression overrides speed and detail.
Fix in staging and run fresh held-out cases; do not train on and reuse the same failed case as sole proof.

cases.prompt: A new MCP server claims much better repository search and ships a prebuilt binary from an unversioned release. Its repository has no clear license or security documentation. Our current search is imperfect. Explain whether and how it can enter the agent surface.
criteria: Refuses live installation or promotion from the unversioned binary.
Requires canonical source, version, license, provenance, and security review before execution.
Compares the current baseline with credible safer alternatives.
Uses isolated staging, representative evaluation, held-out proof, and rollback if a candidate remains viable.

cases.prompt: A skill beat the baseline on both agents six months ago. Since then, both default models, tool policies, and one host's skill loader changed. The skill text is unchanged. Can the old win authorize promotion today? Preserve anything still useful.
criteria: Rejects the old result as current admission proof because relevant runtime variables changed.
Preserves prior results as historical evidence rather than deleting them.
Re-runs current baselines, candidate cases, trigger checks, regressions, and fresh held-out cases on both target hosts.
Limits reevaluation to affected claims and keeps no-change as a valid outcome.
